extracted.intended_audience: TeX/LaTeX users (mathematicians) typesetting matrix-like/commutative diagrams with XY-pic
extracted.subtask_description: Creating matrix-like (e.g., commutative) diagrams in TeX/LaTeX using the XY-pic package, focusing on entries, arrows, labels, spacing, and advanced arrow/target manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading XY-pic
rubrics_metrics.description: Load XY-pic appropriately for your TeX format (e.g., with \usepackage[all]{xy} for LaTeX2e, or \input xy and \xyoption{all} for plain TeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loading \usepackage[all]{xy} will auto-load an appropriate backend driver (pdftex, dvipdfm, dvips) for PDF/PostScript output. For portability or nonstandard facilities request an explicit driver with \xyoption{pdf} or load only features you use. Use \xyoption{v2} or the old-style files to enable v2 compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagram construction with \xymatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagrams are created with \xymatrix{ ... } where entries are laid out in a matrix: entries separated by & and rows by \\.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the diagram as a matrix grid. Empty trailing entries may be omitted. Use braces to surround constructions containing & if the xymatrix appears inside other tabular environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry default mode and entry-start rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are typeset as mathematics (using \textstyle) and are by default centered; entries should not start with a macro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start entries with a nonexpandable character or wrap them in {} (e.g., {}\bullet) to avoid issues. Entry spacing is often large; use *-modifiers to change format/shape of individual entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifying arrows via base entry with \ar
rubrics_metrics.description: All arrows are specified in the base entry where they start, using \ar followed by a target specification; simple relative hops use letter sequence u,d,l,r (e.g., \ar[ur]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinates are logical: arrow line is between centers of base and target and will adapt to entry sizes. Use explicit target formats for more control (see 'More targets').

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow styles with @-style notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Change arrow appearance with \ar@{...} or \ar@style where the @ argument describes tail, shaft, and head (e.g., @{=>}, @{.>}, @{-->}, @{-}, @{}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can specify tail/shaft/head or use prebuilt variants; variants ^ (above), _ (below), 2 (double), 3 (triple) alter placement/duplication. See the tip/shaft character lists for permitted characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels as superscripts/subscripts on arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels on arrows are conceptualized as superscripts (^) and subscripts (_) relative to the arrow direction: ^ places label 'above' and _ 'below' (positions depend only on arrow direction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels default to the midpoint between base and target; enclose complex labels in {..}. Adding a - immediately after ^ or _ requests placement at the center of the actual arrow. Anything (not just math) can be used as a label (see *object).

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaks in arrows and placing labels outside the mesh
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the | character to break an arrow with a label (e.g., \xymatrix@1{A\ar[r]|f&B}) and use the special \hole for an empty break; use @{} invisible arrow style combined with | to place labels outside the matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking allows labels to be placed at specific points or outside the normal matrix; use @{} to create invisible arrows whose breaks carry external labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curving arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: Make arrows curve to avoid entries using @/^/, @/_/, @/_1pc/ or the general @(in,out) notation to specify incoming/outgoing directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can insert a dimension after ^ or _ to adjust bend amount (e.g., @/_1pc/). @(in,out) computes a curve that begins in direction 'in' at the base and ends from direction 'out' at the target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speeding up typesetting with compiled matrices and outlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \CompileMatrices to create temporary compiled versions of matrices to speed typesetting; if problems occur, disable with \xymatrixnocompile or \NoCompileMatrices. \OnlyOutlines omits compiled pictures; \ShowOutlines adds dotted rectangle outlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To allow compilation reliably, start entries with a nonexpandable character or {; compiled files are recreated when matrices change. Use \OnlyOutlines/\ShowOutlines to inspect picture bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit label positioning tokens (<, >, <<, >>, (.n), !{t1;t2})
rubrics_metrics.description: Place labels at specific points along an arrow using tokens inserted between ^/_/| and the label: < (at arrow start), > (at arrow end), <</>> (a bit further in), (.n) (tie to fractional position n between base (0) and target (1)), and !{t1;t2} (place at intersection of arrow with line from t1 to t2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine these tokens and factors; multiple < or > move the label further in; (.n) is useful for precise fractional placement. !{t1;t2} works only for straight arrows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling with arbitrary objects using *object
rubrics_metrics.description: Use *{...} to use arbitrary TeX material as labels/objects; the more general form is *modifiers{text} where modifiers adjust shape/size/boxing (e.g., +, +=, -, -=, [o], [F], [F=], etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A leading + gives default spacing (objects start with no margin). Boxing commands include \txt{...}, \frm{}, \composite{...}, and \hbox{...}. *-combinations allow composed/multi-part objects separated by *.

rubrics_metrics.name: General arrow construction @{tail shaft head}
rubrics_metrics.description: General arrow notation @{...} describes tail, shaft, and head (all three should be included when necessary); tip and shaft components are chosen from restricted character sets and can be composed with variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tip characters include: <, <<, |<, |<<, (, ), ◦, x, +, |, ||, o, etc. Shaft characters include -, ~, ., --, ~~. Variants ^/_/2/3 add above/below/double/triple. Use *object as the head/tail for arbitrary decoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sliding parallel arrows sideways
rubrics_metrics.description: Slide arrows sideways by appending @<dimen> to an arrow command to offset arrows by a TeX dimension (positive slides in the '^' direction, negative in the '_' direction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common offsets like @<1ex>. Abbreviations = and : are provided for - and . with variant forced to 2. If global variant effects are undesired, use local variant definitions variant{tip} or variant{shaft}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target address formats and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Targets can be specified in many formats: relative [r,c] (same as [hop]), absolute "r,c" (row,col), t';t (change base then set target relative), <Dx,Dy> vector, /d dimen/ vector in direction d, and corner offsets (UL, L, DL, U, D, UR, R, DR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the form best suited for the diagram. Many more options exist in the reference manual including absolute/relative angles and relative vectors (d:a(), d:(x,y)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing or overriding a target
rubrics_metrics.description: Overwrite the visual target by appending *object to a target (typesets object at the target then uses it), use +vector/-vector to change the target to a zero-sized one offset by a vector, or !vector to move the center of the target by a vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vectors can be given as <Dx,Dy> or /d dimen/ forms; these let you place zero-sized anchors or shifted targets for fine-tuned positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows passing under (visiting) intermediate entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Make arrows pass under or 'visit' entries by inserting 't (apostrophe followed by a target) for each intermediate entry that should be visited except the last final entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each visited segment can have its own labels. Going under an empty entry leaves a small gap—use compact tricks described in section 3.3 for tighter layouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bending arrows using turns (backquote `)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `d t (backquote + direction + target) for each quarter-turn: each ` describes a straight segment ending in a quarter-turn (multiples of 1/8 circle segments). Default turn radius is 10pt; change it with /R after the `; change turn sense with ^d (anticlockwise) or _d (clockwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One ` per turn; intermediate targets sizes are ignored; if a segment can't be short enough it may point past the target (useful for going around entries). Each segment supports separate labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining new arrow types with \newdir
rubrics_metrics.description: Define directionals with \newdir{directional}{composite} where 'directional' is a sequence of tip or shaft characters and 'composite' is a *-separated list of objects; variants can be defined by adding ^/_/2/3 between \newdir and the first {.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed tip and shaft characters are restricted (tip chars: ><|ox+/()[]␣; shaft chars: - . ~ := etc.). The composite can include !vector to shift components; use this to create complex bespoke tips/tails/shafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual entry formatting with *object
rubrics_metrics.description: Override entry defaults using the *object form to control spacing, boxing, and content (useful for frames, multi-line text, or non-math entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use *\txt{...} to insert text with optional width constraints (\txt<6pc>{...}). To place multi-line text or formatted content, build the entry as a composed *... object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inserting extra entries outside the matrix with \save/\restore
rubrics_metrics.description: Place additional typeset material not part of the matrix using \save t \restore where t is a target; the saved content does not affect the diagram grid but may be positioned relative to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for large comments or annotations. The saved material can include arrows and other XY constructs but does not change the main layout except when based on displaced pseudo-entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix spacing and rotation codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Control overall matrix spacing and defaults by adding codes between \xymatrix and the following {, e.g., @=dimen, @R=dimen, @C=dimen, @M, @W, @H, @L; use +=/+=/-/-= variants to increase/decrease; @! forces equal spacing; @!0 forces fixed grid ignoring entry sizes; @!R/@!C force equal rows/columns; rotate grid with @d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use @=0pt and @M=0pt to compact grids; @! and @!0 are handy to produce fixed grids. Rotation rotates the grid only, not cell contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry style defaults and global modifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Change default entry and label formatting via \objectstyle and \labelstyle (entries default to math textstyle). Change default entry modifiers with \entrymodifiers (e.g., ++[o][F-] to make entries round and framed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set \objectstyle to \hbox to abandon math-mode entries. Use \SelectTips{cm}{} to select tip fonts (cm/eu/lu/xy) and optionally point size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming entries for reuse (targets t=\"name\")
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a named target with t="name" which refers to the target just before the =; named targets can be used later to create arrows to/from complex saved constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when excursions create long constructs you want to reference later (e.g., name frames or composed regions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping/merging objects into single targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use t.s to merge target t with simple s (expanding t to cover s) and {t} to make t simple; merged objects' center corresponds to the original target's center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lets you frame or treat a rectangle of objects as a single object (useful with \save and \restore plus *[F.]\frm{} to create framed blocks and then arrow to them by name).

rubrics_metrics.name: Backwards compatibility mode and known exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A v2 compatibility mode is available (via old-style loading or \xyoption{v2}); compatibility is almost full but some exceptions exist (automatic shortening of arrow tails bug fixed, release 2.6 * position operator not available, certain target syntaxes need bracing, old \pit commands not defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If migrating old diagrams check the listed exceptions and suggested fixes (use |<\hole, replace * position with :/:: operators, brace complex targets, use *@{>} instead of old pit macros). Report other regressions to xy-pic maintainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining XY-pic and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Get XY-pic from CTAN, TeX Live, or the XY-pic home page. XY-pic is distributed under the GNU GPL (version 2 or later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are free to use XY-pic, but distributing parts (including modified versions) requires making full source available per the GPL; see the COPYING file and http://www.gnu.org/licenses/ for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced/auxiliary XY-pic features
rubrics_metrics.description: XY-pic provides additional high-level features: \graph for directed graphs, \2cell for categorical 2-cells, \poly for polygon-like structures, \web for lattice composition, \arc and \knot for arcs and mathematical knots/links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features produce complex figures with relatively few lines; consult the reference manual for details and examples (xysamples on CTAN).
